edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Comm. in Cant. Prologus 10

source_text: His ita praemissis, iam ipsa verba Cantici Canticorum, quantum Dominus dederit, explanare temptemus, orantes ut sponsus ipse, qui haec per Salomonem cecinit, etiam nunc in nobis loquatur et aperiat sensum nostrum ad intellegenda scripturarum mysteria. Incipit ergo liber: Osculetur me ab osculis oris sui. Sed de hoc et sequentibus in ipso Librorum ordine plenius disseretur.
pass_a_gloss: With-these thus having-been-set-first, already themselves words of-Song of-Songs, as-much-as Lord will-have-given, to-explain let-us-attempt, praying that bridegroom himself who these through Solomon sang, also now in us may-speak... Begins therefore book: Let-him-kiss me from kisses of-mouth of-him...
pass_b_english: With these things thus set first, let us now attempt to explain the very words of the Song of Songs, as far as the Lord has given, praying that the Bridegroom himself, who sang these things through Solomon, may even now speak in us and open our sense to understand the mysteries of the Scriptures. The book therefore begins: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth. But of this and of what follows fuller treatment will be given in the order of the Books themselves.
